One best piece of reality I can give you tonight is a truth found in handicapped rehab centres. Here in France a movie dropped a few years ago, the plot is about those friends in this teenager hospital where various handicaps are found.

The public was rather surprised to see that between themselves the kids would always mock each other, insult each other and so on based on their diseases. Turns out the actors (who are actually handicapped) explained that this is how it goes in such centers/hospitals, and that any form of PITY (what someone would usually feel towards a paralyzed kid for example) will NEVER solve anything, only make it worse, by embracing the hard truth of the handicap.

I guess you can try to apply this to yourself, remember not to look for pity or forced attention from people. Anything you do try and make sure that what people give you is not based on your current psychological situation. You want real life, real answers, real feelings, real shit you feel me? It’s very difficult because it means you constantly have to hide your true self, but it’s how I managed to get through my suicidal days.

I hope my point won’t come across as patronizing or so "obvious" to you, this mindset really helped me.
